patch.value: Ordering-evidence tranche: recover sequence edges for terminal work from explicit prerequisite statements already written in item text

Shippable enabling tranche under pm-gxs55a. The ordering half of the graph is degenerate: of 9456 edges only 664 carry sequence, layer_count is 7, and 1771 of 2004 sequenced nodes have no predecessor. pm-lnrk closed the connectivity deficit and explicitly refused to manufacture ordering edges from release cohorts or parent lineage, which was correct: chronology is not causality and a cohort is not a prerequisite. There is however a source of ordering evidence that is neither inferred nor fabricated, because a human or an agent wrote the assertion down in the item itself. Descriptions, comments, notes and close reasons across the corpus contain explicit prerequisite statements naming an identifier: forms such as blocked by, sequence after, lands first and blocks, gated on, prerequisite, waits on, must land before, and depends on. Each such sentence is a recorded claim about order made by the person who knew, and promoting it to a typed edge records what the corpus already says instead of guessing. The tranche extracts those statements, resolves the direction from the sentence rather than from the position of the identifier, drops every candidate whose direction is ambiguous or reversed, and writes the surviving edges as blocked_by. It is changelog-safe under the same rules pm-3j6it6 established, and it is bounded and resumable so the same extractor can run on a million-item corpus.

Candidate ordering edges are extracted only from durable text that names an identifier and states a precedence relation in the sentence itself; Direction is taken from the sentence, and any candidate whose direction is ambiguous or whose sentence names the derived item rather than the prerequisite is dropped rather than resolved by guessing; Every dropped candidate is counted and the drop reasons are reported, so the refusal rate is visible evidence rather than silent filtering; Applied edges are typed blocked_by, create no new cycles, and leave graph audit findings and validate warning classes no worse than before the tranche; The resulting change in ordering depth is measured and reported: predecessor coverage, layer count, and longest ordering path before and after; The extraction runs bounded and resumable so it is executable against a corpus far larger than this workspace
Turn precedence statements the corpus already contains into traversable ordering edges
The project timeline is the part of the graph traversal cannot currently recover; the evidence for much of it is already written down
Connectivity is saturated at one component and zero orphans, which makes ordering depth the next and now the only structural deficit

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
First tranche executed 2026-07-27. Result: 10 edges applied, 20 candidates dropped, and the headline finding is that the ordering deficit is an authoring gap, not an extraction gap.

Method. Two passes over every item document in the workspace (2,131 items, descriptions, acceptance criteria, comments, notes and close reasons).

Pass one, single-endpoint: a precedence phrase followed by an identifier, attributing the other end to the item the sentence lives in. Twenty-one phrase forms, including blocked by, blocked on, gated on, waits on, depends on, prerequisite is, after X lands, sequence after, once X lands, requires X first, X lands first, X blocks this, blocks X, unblocks X, prerequisite for X, must land before X. Forty-two raw matches, 32 distinct ordered pairs, 6 already edged, 26 candidates.

Pass two, two-endpoint: both ends named inside the same sentence, with continuation handling for lists written as X blocked_by Y + Z or Y/Z. Twelve distinct asserted pairs, 5 already edged, 7 candidates.

Applied, 10 edges, each one a sentence in the corpus that names its own prerequisite:
  pm-3hps blocked_by pm-801d      (asserted four times, in two independent notes)
  pm-55ra blocked_by pm-h3no      (asserted twice)
  pm-55ra blocked_by pm-atfm      (asserted twice)
  pm-55ra blocked_by pm-dfg0      (asserted twice)
  pm-114v blocked_by pm-8t5x
  pm-13bn blocked_by pm-7qjk
  pm-9yfo blocked_by pm-klo8      (stated in the item's own acceptance criteria)
  pm-xspd blocked_by pm-zuw8      (stated in the item's own acceptance criteria)
  pm-bgcu blocked_by pm-2muu      (stated in the item's own description)
  pm-hybj blocked_by pm-iqgj

Dropped, 20 candidates, in three named classes. The drop rate is 67 percent and the classes matter more than the count, because each one is a way a naive extractor silently fabricates.

Class one, hub-note misattribution, 14 candidates. Roadmap and pass-summary items accumulate notes that report edges between other items. A sentence on pm-doxj reading "it now blocks pm-e9zh" is about pm-pcys9n, not about pm-doxj, but a single-endpoint extractor attributes it to the item it is reading and invents pm-e9zh blocked_by pm-doxj. Every candidate whose subject was pm-doxj, pm-4k6b, pm-e9yevx, pm-89qv6b or pm-o043 fell in this class. On a corpus with review-pass notes this is the dominant failure mode, and it is invisible without reading the sentence.

Class two, continuation over-reach, 2 candidates. A comma-separated list is not always a continuation. In "pm-9rgaal blocked_by pm-j82fd3, pm-t4d7nz blocked_by pm-xp1xsw", the comma begins a new clause, and treating it as a continuation of the first prerequisite list produces pm-9rgaal blocked_by pm-t4d7nz, which is backwards.

Class three, over-broad scope, 4 candidates. A sentence that gates one part of an item is not a claim about the item. "Catalog entries (14), (15) and (17) are gated on pm-vvib acceptance" does not make the whole relevance engine blocked by the ADR, and its wave one shipped.

Adjacent extraction confirmed saturated, so it should not be re-attempted. Thirty-five "superseded by" assertions exist and 51 of the 54 supersedes edges are already applied; the three apparent gaps are hub-note misattribution again. Thirteen lineage assertions were found for discovered_from and none survived review: the phrases that generate them, "sibling of" and "class precedent", assert similarity rather than derivation and belong to related, which they already carry.

Consequence for the parent item. Ten honest ordering edges exist in a corpus of 2,131 items spanning months. That is the whole harvest, and it is not a limitation of the extractor: the sentences simply are not there. Precedence is stated in prose roughly once per two hundred items. So the remedy for the flat ordering graph cannot be a better extractor over the existing corpus. It has to be capture at write time, which makes this tranche the end of the extraction approach and the evidence for choosing the other one.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Blocking finding 2026-07-31, filed as pm-xm0id4: this tranche cannot ship as specified, and the reason is a defect rather than a scoping problem.

The acceptance criteria require that applied edges are typed blocked_by, and the target population is terminal work. clearClosedBlockerSignals in src/cli/commands/close.ts:626 deletes every blocked_by row on an item when that item is closed - unconditionally, without regard to the blocker's status. So every edge this tranche recovers lands on a closed item and is one lifecycle transition from being deleted again: a reopen followed by a reclose erases the recovered tranche silently, and the only signal is a single closed_cleared_blocked_by warning that names one blocker even when several were removed (pm-scbr0s).

The corpus already shows the outcome of writing ordering this way. Of 1,900 closed items exactly one retains a blocked_by row; the untouched reverse spelling blocks survives on 189. Any extraction that writes blocked_by onto terminal work is writing into the one field the lifecycle clears.

This does not invalidate the tranche's core argument, which remains correct and valuable: explicit prerequisite statements written in item text are recorded claims rather than inferences, and promoting them to typed edges records what the corpus already says. What it invalidates is the storage target. Either pm-xm0id4 changes the retention semantics first, in which case this tranche proceeds unchanged and should be sequenced behind it, or the recovered edges are written in a form the close path does not clear, which is a decision this tranche should not make alone because it affects the whole ordering vocabulary that pm-4020c5 owns.

Recommended sequencing: hold this tranche behind pm-xm0id4 rather than reworking its extraction design, since the extraction half is sound and independently reviewable. A blocked_by edge to pm-xm0id4 has been recorded.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Blocker state and corpus measurement re-read live 2026-08-01. Of this item's two recorded blockers, pm-xm0id4 is now CLOSED and delivered ('changed the default close path to clear transient blocked scalars while preserving blocked_by dependency rows ... durable predecessor-edge lifecycle semantics ... through close/reopen/reclose'). Only pm-wrbe remains open. The reason this tranche was unsafe to execute -- that any recovered ordering edge written onto a terminal item would be deleted the next time that item transitioned -- no longer holds. Corpus measured structurally over all 1,913 closed items via pm list --status closed --full --json rather than by grep, because 'blocked_by' appears in prose on many items and a text match overcounts by roughly fiftyfold: 8 closed items retain a blocked_by dependency row (up from the 1 measured on 2026-07-31, so the fix is taking effect prospectively), 186 carry the reverse blocks spelling that the close path never touched, and all 1,913 carry at least one dependency of some kind, so there are no dependency-isolates among terminal items -- the deficit is specifically ordering, not connectivity. The recovery target is therefore the gap between 8 recorded predecessors and the 186-plus prerequisites recorded from the opposite endpoint, plus whatever the history streams hold for edges deleted before the fix landed.
